title: Zephyrine and the Bridge
premise: Sebastian Kavanagh, a nurse at the Ashcombe military hospital in 1871, has spent twelve years recording the names of dead soldiers that officers strike from official ledgers — a quiet act of justice outside the law. When a dying courier presses a sealed letter into her hands, naming the influential Marlowe family as architects of a supply-robbery scandal that starved a whole regiment, Sebastian discovers her own late brother's name among the silenced. To deliver the evidence to a parliamentary inquiry before it is destroyed, she must smuggle the letter past three checkpoints with the help of Captain Elias Thorne, the Marlowes' own son, whose loyalty to family and love for Sebastian tear him in opposite directions. At the final checkpoint Elias chooses truth over blood, testifying against his father; the Marlowes fall, Sebastian's ledger is read aloud in Parliament, and she and Elias leave together to build a hospital where no name is ever erased.
about_author: Rosalind Underhill is a former archivist from Yorkshire who spent a decade cataloguing regimental records before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for unearthing the quiet, undocumented lives of women who kept the empire's ledgers.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At Ashcombe hospital she tends the wounded by day and, by candlelight, adds a dead private's name to her hidden ledger of the officially forgotten. We learn her rules: never copy, never speak, never trust an officer. Emotional beat: weary, disciplined tenderness — and the first crack, when a dying man whispers a name she recognizes.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed in Black Wax
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A courier, feverish and shot through the shoulder, dies on her ward after pressing a sealed letter into her apron and saying only 'Marlowe' and 'the bridge at Vellacourt.' She reads it against every instinct: it names the Marlowe family in the supply robbery that starved the 44th. Emotional beat: dread and recognition — her brother Thomas died with the 44th.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with a flashback to 1859. She recalls how Thomas's name vanished from the casualty rolls and how she began her ledger. Now the letter offers proof of why the 44th was starved. She must decide by morning whether to burn it or carry it to the inquiry in London. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Captain Who Drinks Alone
chapters.summary: Elias Thorne's POV. Captain Elias Thorne, the Marlowes' estranged son serving at Ashcombe, notices Sebastian burning papers and confronts her. She lies; he half-believes her. He is drinking to forget his father's letters demanding his silence. Emotional beat: two guarded people circling each other, each hiding half a truth.

chapters.title: Orders from Ashcombe House
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A summons from his father, Sir Aldous Marlowe, orders him to search the hospital for 'stolen correspondence.' He realizes his family is hunting the letter — and that the nurse may have it. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: An Alliance of Necessity
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She tests Elias by showing him a single page; his horror at his father's signature convinces her. They agree: he will get her past the first checkpoint at the Vellacourt bridge in three days, when the mail coach runs. Emotional beat: fragile trust, struck like a match in a dark room.

chapters.title: The Matron's Price
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Matron Grigg, who has quietly protected the ledger for years, warns that an informer walks the wards. She gives Sebastian a nurse's traveling pass and her own brother's name to use — then asks for one thing: that Thomas's name be spoken aloud someday. Emotional beat: sisterhood of the silenced; the cost of asking.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Toll House
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Sebastian, disguised as a nurse escorting a coffin, passes the toll house where a sergeant with the Marlowe crest checks papers. Elias creates a diversion — a staged quarrel — that nearly turns real when the sergeant recognizes him. Emotional beat: terror braided with the first electric awareness between them.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Vellacourt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Waiting at the bridge where Thomas last marched, she tells Elias about her brother. He confesses he signed, years ago, the requisition order that falsified the 44th's supply returns — believing it was clerical. Emotional beat: confession as intimacy; love beginning exactly where guilt lives.

chapters.title: A Father's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A letter reaches him on the road: Sir Aldous knows the letter survived and names Sebastian. Elias burns the summons and lies by wire to his father — his first open act of betrayal. Emotional beat: the exhilaration and nausea of crossing a line that cannot be uncrossed.

chapters.title: The Informer's Face
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In a coaching inn she comes face to face with the informer — Orderly Penn, a man whose son's name is in her ledger. He begs her to understand: the Marlowes hold his debts. She offers him a page of the letter to copy as insurance. Emotional beat: pity and fury in the same breath; justice outside the law gets complicated.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The River Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The river gate checkpoint demands to open every case. The letter, sewn into a dead soldier's uniform in the coffin, is nearly found — until Elias produces his commission and stakes his name on it. Emotional beat: Elias spends his honor as currency, and both know it cannot be spent twice.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A sleepless night in a hayloft; he drafts and burns three letters to his father. Sebastian wakes and finds him, and they speak plainly of love for the first time — and of what it will cost. Emotional beat: tenderness with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Moves Up
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A newspaper reveals the parliamentary inquiry has been abruptly adjourned — the Marlowes have bought themselves a fortnight, and a sympathetic chairman. The evidence must now reach a backbencher, Mr. Calloway, not the committee. Emotional beat: the ground shifting; hope rerouted through humbler doors.

chapters.title: Penn's Choice
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Orderly Penn intercepts them at a crossroads — sent to retrieve the letter — and instead hands Sebastian the Marlowes' route schedule, then turns back to face his creditors alone. Emotional beat: a small, unsung act of courage; the ledger's philosophy vindicated.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: Ashcombe's Own Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The final checkpoint is not a barrier but Sir Aldous himself, waiting at the London terminus. Elias walks up to his father, hands him the letter — a decoy, the real evidence hidden in Sebastian's ledger of names — and lets himself be taken. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as surrender.

chapters.title: The Room Where Names Are Read
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. While Elias is held at his father's house, Sebastian reaches Calloway and reads her twelve-year ledger aloud in his study: name after name, ending with Thomas Kavanagh. Calloway, moved and pragmatic, agrees to force the inquiry to reopen. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into testimony; the quiet made thunderous.

chapters.title: The Trial of a Son
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Sir Aldous offers Elias freedom and the family name if he recants and names Sebastian as a thief. In the study where he grew up, Elias refuses — and tells his father he will testify. Emotional beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth; a son outgrowing his father's shadow.

chapters.title: Before the Committee
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. At the reopened inquiry, Elias testifies against his own family, corroborated by the ledger and Penn's copied page. Sir Aldous's counsel collapses; the chairman who was bought is exposed. Emotional beat: catharsis — justice arriving not as a sword but as paperwork, read aloud by ordinary voices.

chapters.title: Aftermath at Ashcombe
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Marlowes' fall ripples outward; the 44th's dead are officially restored to the rolls. Sebastian visits Thomas's restored name on the memorial wall and leaves a copy of the ledger page. Emotional beat: mourning that finally has somewhere to rest.

chapters.title: The Bridge, Rebuilt
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Elias, stripped of his commission but cleared of dishonor, meets Sebastian at Vellacourt bridge, where a new span is being raised. He gives her the one thing he kept: his father's original confession, for her ledger. Emotional beat: love chosen freely, with nothing left to hide.

chapters.title: A Hospital Where No Name Is Erased
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, coda. A year later, the Kavanagh-Thorne convalescent hospital opens its doors; above the matron's desk hangs the ledger, bound and public, its first page Thomas's name. Sebastian writes a new first entry in a fresh book. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won hope — justice institutionalized, love made ordinary and daily.
